_comment: Pressure/density altitude. The two KULM and KLUM cases are REFERENCE VALUES published by Garmin Pilot in its Aug 20 2026 briefing PDF - an independent implementation - and our moist-air method matches them to within 25 ft. The dry elevation+120*(OAT-ISA) rule of thumb misses both by ~260 ft LOW, and understating density altitude is the dangerous direction. Tolerance is +/-30 ft to absorb Garmin publishing integer temps.

cases.why: Garmin published 1586 ft. Altimeter 30.05 inHg = 1017.6 hPa. Near-saturated, so the humidity correction matters.
Garmin published 1170 ft. Altimeter 30.07 inHg = 1018.3 hPa. Fully saturated (temp == dewpoint).
REGRESSION ANCHOR (not an external reference). Hot and high: a 5431 ft field on a 31C day yields a density altitude ~2850 ft above field elevation.
REGRESSION ANCHOR (not an external reference). The live demo flight: 38C at DFW puts density altitude ~2900 ft above the 607 ft field - a real factor for a loaded heavy.
